**Description**
Millions of sellers list products on Amazon. You'll own the services that tell them what a valid listing needs, get their submissions live, and explain what to fix when one fails.
  
  
Selling on Amazon comes down to three things a seller has to get right: learn what a valid listing needs, get it submitted, and fix it when something goes wrong. We build for all three, in every marketplace where Amazon operates. Some of our services tell a seller what their category requires before they submit, and whether their product is already in our catalog. Others take listings in and update them, one at a time or thousands at once in a bulk feed, and carry them through to a live offer. When something breaks, ours are the services that say what went wrong, in the seller's own language, while there's still time to fix it.
  
  
You'll work on software that every seller and every seller tool passes through. The problems are API design, concurrency, event-driven processing, and data modeling over a catalog whose rules shift by product, by marketplace, and by seller. You'll own what you build, from design through production and the on-call rotation that follows, on a team cutting years of overlapping systems down to fewer and simpler ones. There's room to grow into owning a system end to end.

* Operate what you build. Take part in an on-call rotation, hold the line on the latency and availability sellers depend on, drive issues to a permanent root cause fix, and automate recurring work instead of absorbing it.

* Work with the customers and partner teams that depend on your services, and make priority calls between new features, operational work, and business commitments. Keep your tools current, including AI-assisted development, and stay accountable for the quality of everything you ship.

You Join a Team Of Six To Twelve Engineers, With a Manager And Senior Engineers Who Read Your Designs And Your Code. A Typical Day Looks Like This
  
  

* Participating in stand-ups, sprint planning, and retrospectives
* Writing, testing, and debugging code for ongoing projects
* Reviewing code and incorporating feedback from your team
* Collaborating on technical solutions in design and architecture reviews
* Working with stakeholders to understand requirements
* Monitoring existing systems and resolving production issues
* Documenting technical specifications and processes
* Learning and applying new technologies and best practices

Sellers are on the other end of all of it. A change you write this month is something a seller runs into next month, and the feedback comes back fast.

**About SDI**

SDI is a healthcare AI startup building surgical decision-support tools for spine surgery. Founded by practicing spine surgeons and academic faculty, we combine deep clinical expertise with modern machine learning to improve surgical planning and patient outcomes. Our platform spans medical imaging pipelines, clinical outcomes data, and ML models that operate on both.

**The role**

Our early research has found strong signals in spine MRI for predicting what happens to patients after imaging and after surgery. The job now is to build on that foundation: test the findings rigorously, extend them, and turn them into validated models running in our product. It needs to be done carefully enough that surgeons, journals and regulators will trust the results.

You’ll work closely with our clinical research lab, our founding surgeons and the AI/ML team. The problems range widely, from questions that need large-scale clinical data and careful study design to open methods problems in learning from 3D medical imaging. You’ll turn them into well-designed studies, models and code, and be able to tell when the data supports an answer and when it doesn’t. We expect you to go deep on the math when a problem calls for it, and to publish where it supports our goals.

Expect to spend roughly half your time on research and half on the engineering that makes it reproducible and shippable: building reproducible cohorts and training data, and writing training and evaluation code that others can run and build on. As our data foundations mature, the balance will shift toward research. On a team this small, research that can’t be reproduced or deployed doesn’t help anyone.

**What you’ll work on**

**Problems on our roadmap include:**

* **Outcomes and durability prediction.**
  Combine imaging features, segmentations and foundation-model embeddings with clinical and surgical data to predict how patients will do, including which patients are likely to need further treatment.
* **Representation learning for 3D MRI.**
  Self-supervised and foundation models for volumetric, multi-sequence spine MRI, where the anisotropy and multiple contrasts break assumptions built for 2D images.
* **Spatial prediction from imaging.**
  Predict where pathology and future events are likely, such as heat maps over the spine, not only whether they will occur.
* **Labels and expert disagreement.**
  Our labels come from radiologists and surgeons, and experts disagree. Model that disagreement, and decide which cases experts should label next.
* **Quantitative imaging biomarkers.**
  Make measurements comparable across scanners and sites: harmonization, test-retest agreement, and calibrated uncertainty.
* **Study design.**
  Build reproducible, leakage-free cohorts, and handle censoring, confounding and selection bias in real-world clinical data.
* **Learning across sites.**
  Models that keep adapting as new hospitals, scanners and pathologies come online, without forgetting what they’ve learned.
* **Evaluation and interpretability.**
  Evaluate models against the costs of real errors on ordinal grading scales, and test whether explanations of model behavior hold up.
* **Clinical NLP.**
  Extract and organize what’s in radiology reports, operative notes and clinic notes, and summarize a patient’s record into a concise spine health summary.

**Engineering.**
Write research code that others can run and extend. Track experiments and register models in MLflow. Work with the rest of the AI/ML team to move models from experiment to production in days rather than months. Publish where it supports our goals, in clinical spine journals and at venues like MICCAI, and contribute the research side of our FDA software-as-a-medical-device work.

**What we’re looking for**

* A Ph.D. in a technical field such as machine learning, computer science, applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology or biomedical engineering, with research focused on clinical or radiology problems. Ideally you’ve spent substantial time embedded in a clinical or radiology research group, working directly with real patient data and with physicians.
* Hands-on experience building ML models on medical imaging, ideally MRI, in Python and PyTorch. You write the code yourself.
* Statistical and mathematical depth. You’re comfortable with survival and time-to-event analysis, causal inference, and how to evaluate a model properly, and you can derive and reason about a method rather than only apply one.
* Experience designing clinical studies or validation studies, and an understanding of why real-world clinical data misleads people.
* Comfort working directly with physicians: you can understand their reasoning, challenge it constructively, and explain technical results in terms they can act on.
* Software engineering habits: version control, tests, reproducible experiments, and code other people depend on.
* A track record of research that reached the real world, through a product, a clinical tool, or work that others built on.

**Nice to have**

* Musculoskeletal or spine imaging, or orthopedic or neurosurgical research.
* Clinical NLP or LLMs applied to medical records: radiology reports, operative notes, information extraction and summarization.
* Experience with inter-rater reliability, latent-variable label models, active learning or decision-curve analysis.
* Representation learning and foundation models for medical imaging (e.g., DINO-style self-supervised learning).
* MRI physics and harmonization across scanners and protocols.
* Regulated medical software: FDA SaMD, clinical validation, HIPAA.
* Peer-reviewed publications in clinical journals and in ML or medical imaging venues.

**What this role is not**

* Not open-ended academic research. Publishing is encouraged, but the work has to make it into our product.
* Not an MLOps or platform role. You’ll write code with production in mind and work closely with the team that ships it, but infrastructure and serving aren’t your job.
* Not a role where you work alone on the clinical side. You’ll have strong clinical partners at HSS and on our advisory council. You won’t need to be the clinical expert, but you’ll need to speak their language.
